[WP] Every user on Voat is actually a perfect clone of their Reddit counterpart.

I'm a fairly conservative user of the Internet. I have a Facebook account, though I don't post much. I have a Twitter account, though my following of 13 people doesn't amount to much. Also, I have a Voat account and a Reddit account. Or at least, that's what I used to think.

Reddit was abuzz, filled with more drama than a hallway full of eighth-graders, and with great resignation I decided to explore my options for the Exodus. Stumbling upon a stray comment, I found Voat, its sleek interface and built-in nightmode and image viewer gently carressing my browsing experience like I never knew I needed.

This is is it, I thought to myself. This is the new site.

My fingers flew in a blur, a frenzied clicking and clacking dancing across the keyboard as I eagerly searched for my favorite content to contribute to Voat. In less than fifteen minutes, I had compiled a picture of screenshots from teenage girls who misspelled the word 'colon' for cologne.

The perfect start, I couldn't help thinking to myself, cringing at colon tweets all the while. One click was all it took to submit.

Suddenly, it occurred to me. What if this is a repost from Reddit? Won't people here just think that I'm some lame content thief? In my panic, I opened up a new tab for the old site, pausing only to notice the small orange envelope standing meekly in the corner of my screen. A user had commented on something I submitted..?

Impossible. I haven't posted anything in months, apart from commenting the occasional Lenny face when the opportunity arose.

Curiosity getting the better of me, I clicked it. Someone named LemonParty451 had commented on my colon post! Getting attention already was amazing. I thought to myself how if you could get attention that quickly, Voat would be–

Hang on. The Snoo stared at me from the corner, almost with a hint of betrayal in its pale white face. I was still on Reddit. What in hell was going on here? Flipping back quickly to Voat, a little red notification appeared on my screen. Who else would it be, but LemonParty451.

I was confused. Mystified. Maybe some loser was stalking me, but you'd have to be a real loser to be stalking another loser; let's be real here. With my curiousity piqued, I decided to cross-reference Voat and Reddit. Every single user on Voat was... an identical clone of a user on Reddit? I started to wonder if I had ever created a Reddit account in the first place. How could mirrors be real if our eyes aren't real?

This had to be some elaborate hoax. But how? It had happened to me too. I posted against the rules in /r/funny and /v/funny. The posts were deleted. At the same three minute, forty-second mark.

This was amazing. Whoever, or whatever – was doing this, I couldn't possibly understand why. But none of that mattered to me now. I had them to thank.

Now – now, I could shitpost twice as efficiently. ( ͡~ ͜ʖ ͡°)

How can you declare a show "garbage" in a way that is "statistically speaking"? Which statistics are you talking about?

I think Attack on Titan was not well paced, for sure, but it was still entertaining. Also, something that brings another wave of fans in can't be without merits.

First, I rate shows on a logarithmic scale, with a 5/10 defined as "average." Or in other words, it's a show that exists, but it fails to stand out from the crowd for either good or bad reasons.

Secondly, "garbage" here is not meant to imply whether or not the show is enjoyable. I watch plenty of shows I think are garbage. Shows are judged as garbage when they are unlikely to excel in most of the five categories I judge a show on, which are: concept, story, characters, aesthetics, and execution.

So let's talk statistics and anime, and how it applies to Attack on Titan.

Conceptually, it's an action-oriented series, based on a group that gets itself involved in a military squad to defend a wall against an evil force that lurks outside a protected wall -- in this case specifically, giants.

First off, action series are notoriously filled with garbage shows (which again, doesn't imply that they aren't entertaining, they just fail to stand out from their peers). It's just too easy to use action as a crutch for bad writing. Fortunately action is not the worst offender here -- just one of them.

Secondly, let's break down and find some shows that have similar themes and motifs. For the cases of a militarized units (even if not military themselves) defending a wall or barrier, we have Chrome Shelled Regios. You have a squad of kids -- some with troubled backgrounds -- who defend a walled city from an evil force outside the town. So one of the major concepts here has been done, and done reasonably well.

Next, let's get into some spoilers, so avert your eyes for a bit.

So what is the point of this? Conceptually, the show really doesn't stand out. A lot of its key elements have been done in some variation or another by another show previously. This isn't to say that the show can't be enjoyed nor that it can't be good, but that the deck is slightly stacked against it -- especially since most of the examples I listed are shows that I would also consider garbage. Enjoyable, but largely forgettable in the grand scheme of things. There is also no reasonable expectation, from what I've read of the series, for the show to do any better than the examples I listed. Thus, statistically speaking, it is garbage.
